title: History 14: The speed era: LCM, turbo and distillation

questions.q: Plain Euler with a perfect model gets 1.39 at one call, and the student gets 0.14. What did the student learn that Euler doesn't have?
options: Where the path from this point ends, rather than its direction at this point
questions.answer: Where the path from this point ends, rather than its direction at this point
questions.why: Euler moves along the local direction once and lands on an average. The student was trained on end points.

questions.q: In LCM.calculate_denoised, what does the output equal at timestep 0?
options: Exactly the input, because c_skip is 1 and c_out is 0
questions.answer: Exactly the input, because c_skip is 1 and c_out is 0
questions.why: That boundary rule is built into the formula, so training cannot break it.

questions.q: What does cfg 1 do to the number of calls?
options: Halves them, since sampling_function skips the negative branch
questions.answer: Halves them, since sampling_function skips the negative branch
questions.why: So 4 steps at cfg 1 is 4 calls, against 40 for 20 steps at cfg 7.

questions.q: The same student meets data with the hump weights swapped. What happens, and why?
options: The error jumps to 1.37, since a student copies one teacher's answers
It stays at 0.14, since the data is similar
questions.answer: The error jumps to 1.37, since a student copies one teacher's answers
questions.why: It only knows where that teacher's paths ended. Nothing in it looks at new data.

questions.q: At 4 steps, what does SDTurboScheduler pick?
options: A list read from the checkpoint
questions.why: It takes the first steps of a fixed list, so more steps do not mean a finer walk to low noise.
